title: Seismic discards an unsaved interpretation after a failed save or cancelled conflict
kind: Confirmed defect; real UI failure injection
explanation: save_now returns False on SQLite/OSError and on conflict Cancel. close_project ignores it, calls close_survey (which clears interp), destroys windows and closes the database. select_survey likewise ignores False. on_close destroys the application in finally even if closing raises. Layout is saved before the interpretation, so a fresh database modification time need not mean picks were saved.
repro: Run probes/ui_cases.py. Open the synthetic SEG-Y project, set Horizon 1[6,8]=1000 and save. Change it to 1200; inject sqlite3.OperationalError from store.save_interpretation; close and reopen.
expected: Abort close/survey switch and retain the live interpretation until a successful save or explicit discard.
actual: Project closes despite the save error; reopened pick is 1000, not 1200. Separate status text says work stays in the window, but close removes that window.
v69: Reproduced identically on 020a48d; the v0.9.70 cleanup is after the same unchecked save.
regression: Automate disk-full/I/O/locked-commit failure and conflict Cancel through Close Project, WM close and survey/project switch. Assert dirty objects/window/database remain, then retry and verify fresh-process stored values.
fix: Honor a single save outcome before any close, switch, callback cancellation or destruction; preserve state on failure/Cancel. Remove unconditional destroy on failed close. Show an actionable persistent failure.
recovery: Previously committed picks remain. Never-committed edits are normally recoverable only while the process still holds them; a WAL cannot recover edits never written to SQLite.

title: Geosteering treats a failed autosave as permission to discard a saved/project job
kind: Confirmed defect; real UI failure injection
explanation: _confirm_discard flushes a pending autosave, but then returns True whenever job.path is set or in_project is True even if dirty remains True after that save failed. If an earlier autosave has already failed and cleared its timer, the same condition skips a retry. on_close releases resources and destroys the window.
repro: Run probes/close_errors.py. Save a synthetic project job named Saved, change its name to Unsaved, mark_dirty, inject SQLite write failure in geosteering.project.save_job, then on_close and reload the job.
expected: Keep the dirty job open after failure or require explicit informed discard.
actual: The project closes and stored job name remains Saved; Unsaved is lost. _autosave only sets a status message before closing.
v69: Reproduced identically on 020a48d; file unchanged in v0.9.70.
regression: Test pending autosave failure and already-failed autosave with no pending timer; test standalone .ogsteer and project jobs, lateral/job switch and close; verify segments/faults/targets as well as name.
fix: Make autosave report success and require dirty=False or explicit discard before releasing a job. Saved-path/project membership must not imply dirty work is durable.
recovery: Older saved job/track survives; the failed newer interpretation may exist only in process memory. Preserve any still-running session before further actions.

title: Geo Save Project reports all changes saved while dirty header edits remain; window Exit drops them
explanation: Save Project commits the connection but does not save dirty tabs, then reports All changes are saved as you work. Close Project invokes the dirty resolver, but window Exit/on_close bypasses it and closes the database.
repro: Run probes/ui_cases.py. Load Tab Well, change the header well_name StringVar to Edited Draft, verify dirty(), invoke save_project and then on_close. Query wells from a new connection.
expected: Save Project writes pending edits or states what remains unsaved; Exit invokes the same dirty resolver as Close Project.
actual: Stored name is Tab Well after Save Project and after Exit; dirty-dialog call count is zero. Source emits the all-saved message.
v69: Reproduced identically on 020a48d; relevant files unchanged.
regression: Exercise header/location/manual-data tabs through Save Project, menu Exit, WM close, Close Project and project switch. Test Save/Discard/Cancel and invalid fields; read database after process restart.
fix: Use one dirty-save/close coordinator for the main tabs and owned windows; only report all-saved when all relevant writers succeeded.
recovery: The old well row is preserved. Unsaved form contents generally have no database/WAL copy after destruction.

title: Opening an existing manifest with a missing database silently creates an empty project
explanation: Manifest resolution supplies its database path without checking that the existing project target exists. sqlite3.connect uses create-if-missing behavior. When DB/ exists but its database has not synced, opening the manifest creates a new valid empty schema instead of reporting an incomplete project.
repro: Run probes/ui_cases.py. Create only the normal manifest/folders in a disposable location (never remove an existing database), then open that manifest through SeismicWorkbench.
expected: Open Existing refuses a missing manifest target and leaves the directory unchanged; explicit New Project can create it.
actual: A new database is created and opened with zero wells. This is not overwrite of an existing database, but creates a competing empty artifact in a sync directory.
v69: Reproduced identically on 020a48d; path/database layer unchanged.
regression: Open a manifest with absent DB file, unavailable repository/drive, partial folder transfer and database path outside root. Assert no new DB/sidecars and a clear missing-target error; retain New Project creation tests.
fix: Separate explicit create from open-existing, validate resolved manifest target, and open-existing with no-create SQLite semantics. Show the exact manifest and resolved database path.
recovery: An empty replacement does not prove original data was deleted. Preserve it separately; locate the desktop DB, older versions, conflicted/alternate paths and matching sidecars without overwriting anything.

title: Synced replicas lack a consistent snapshot handoff or stale-generation acceptance check
kind: Confirmed architectural safeguard gap; conditional WAL and independent-replica risks reproduced; Dropbox incident unproven
functions: SessionLock.holder/acquire; open_project; write_project_copy; ProjectDatabase connection/change_stamps; watch_close
explanation: SQLite protects connections to one local database, not independent replicated files. Advisory per-module lock markers can lag synchronization and can be overridden; acquire itself overwrites the marker. No sync-complete/snapshot manifest, conflicted-copy reconciliation or last-accepted remote generation check was found in these project-open/save paths. change_stamps protects derived caches, not cross-computer handoff. App does not explicitly enable WAL; an inherited WAL remains possible.
repro: Run probes/sqlite_scenarios.py: independent copies retain values 30 and 40; selecting a preserved older generation opens value 2 without warning. In explicit WAL mode, committed 99 is missing from a main-only copy (30); abrupt exit with committed 123 leaves main-only at 99; a disposable main+WAL pair recovers 123. Foreign marker is detected but acquire overwrites it.
expected: A supported handoff delivers a verified consistent committed snapshot and rejects incomplete/missing targets; simultaneous editing is explicitly unsupported or coordinated independently of file sync.
actual: Stale/incomplete copies can be accepted. Default DELETE committed-idle main-only copy retained value 2; do not generalize the conditional WAL failure to the default mode or claim Dropbox actually chose a stale file.
v69: Same storage/project/lock paths in 020a48d. v0.9.70 only cancels the handoff polling callback when a window is destroyed.
regression: Automate A–E in both DELETE/WAL, WAL without SHM, delayed sidecars/manifest/assets, independent replicas, split generation, stale/conflicted names and concurrent marker acquisition. Validate target hash/interpretation payload, not mtime alone.
fix: Define single-writer snapshot handoff using SQLite backup plus a versioned manifest/checksums and explicit success acknowledgement. Validate completeness/identity at destination, make concurrent-use policy explicit, and never auto-merge SQLite replicas or checkpoint a live synced original.
recovery: Newest committed data may remain on desktop, in matching WAL, versions or conflicted copies. Preserve each generation intact; do not copy arbitrary sidecars from another generation or choose winners by timestamps.

title: Drawing Finish clears editable vertices before the database write succeeds
kind: Confirmed defect; real UI failure injection for new polygon; same ordering in edited shape
explanation: finish captures nodes and calls cancel before validation/dialog/write. finish_edit similarly cancels before drawings.save. A database error propagates after the editor has already discarded its draft. Normal successful Finish commits through db.execute before tree/grid refresh.
repro: Run probes/drawing_failure.py. Digitize three polygon vertices in a disposable regular Map, inject OperationalError in drawings.save, invoke Finish.
expected: Keep the draft and editing mode on write failure, allowing retry or explicit discard.
actual: Write error propagates, persisted row count is zero, nodes becomes [] and state becomes None. Test did not simulate a user Cancel or unfinished draft close.
v69: finish/finish_edit bodies unchanged from 020a48d; the new disposal logic is not the source of this ordering.
regression: New/edit polygon, fault polygon, contour and external shape destination: inject validation/write/publication failure; assert original and draft vertices survive and retry writes once.
fix: Validate and persist first; only clear the active editing state after confirmed success. Restore or retain draft on all save errors and Cancel from subsidiary destination dialogs.
recovery: Original persisted geometry survives a failed edit; a never-written new polygon normally has no recoverable DB record. Do not confuse post-commit UI hangs with this pre-commit failure.

title: Correlation and Cross Section close after logging failed session/section persistence
kind: Confirmed Correlation/Cross Section UI failures; additional Map line error-reporting path static
explanation: Correlation catches session-save exceptions and logs, then closes. Cross Section autosave catches all exceptions and close destroys regardless. Named and Last section saves are separate transactions. Map section-line save similarly logs a failure while keeping the in-memory visual change. No user retry/discard decision is required.
repro: Run probes/close_errors.py. Save Correlation spacing 1.25, change to 7.25 and fail save_session during close: stored 1.25. Save named section view.top=111, change to 222 and fail save_section during close: stored 111, window destroyed.
expected: Keep the unsaved session/section open or clearly offer retry/discard; save coupled named/Last state consistently.
actual: Older session/section reappears after reopen with warning only in logs. Cross Section section-local correlations/faults/fills can also be inside this JSON; project top/fault picks already committed through shared APIs are a separate store.
v69: Both UI failures reproduced identically on 020a48d; cited files/functions unchanged.
regression: Test close, new/open section, named/Last second-write failure, and Map line-save failure. Verify JSON payloads on fresh reopen plus visible error and retained dirty state.
fix: Return and honor save outcomes; preserve state and notify users. Wrap coupled section saves in one transaction. Apply the same outcome contract to Map line/settings saves.
recovery: Old committed layouts remain; never-saved section-local annotations may be memory-only. A logged error is useful evidence but does not restore the discarded data.

title: Recovery read-only open may create a shared-memory sidecar on the original
kind: Confirmed synthetic filesystem side effect; no user file opened
explanation: mode=ro prevents SQL updates to the main DB, but SQLite can create/write WAL shared memory when the directory is writable. Recovery first tries that connection on the supplied path; its private-copy recovery fallback is reached only after an error. Therefore read-only is not a guarantee of zero filesystem side effects.
repro: Run probes/sqlite_scenarios.py. On a disposable committed WAL pair with no SHM, instantiate ReadOnlyProject and inspect directory entries before/while open.
expected: A forensic zero-touch mode performs all SQLite work on a working copy and preserves original files byte-for-byte.
actual: probe.ogwdb-shm is created on the supplied synthetic path; the WAL value 123 is readable. No main-file SQL write was alleged. Existing recovery tests do not cover this absent-SHM/writable-directory combination.
regression: Hash/list main, WAL, SHM and journal before/after on writable/read-only directories, missing SHM and hot journal, with a writer present. Assert the original is never opened by SQLite for forensic inspection.
fix: Offer explicit copy-first forensic inspection and document normal read-only reader side effects. Do not use immutable=1 as a blanket solution: ignoring WAL can omit committed data.
recovery: Use preserved raw evidence plus a separate disposable working copy. Existing private-copy recovery/backup can be useful there; never checkpoint, repair or open the live original merely to inspect it.

title: The v0.9.70 Drawings layout regression still fails at scaling 1.25 on the audit platform
kind: Confirmed Linux/Tk test failure; Windows impact and exact remaining geometry cause unverified
confidence: High for test failure; Medium for operational exposure
explanation: The shipped bounded event-drain test reaches 20,000 events instead of settling at scaling 1.25. It fails in the combined run and alone. This prevents accepting the Tk fix as fully verified on this platform; it is not evidence that persisted interpretation rows disappeared.
repro: Run the exact isolated Tk recheck in Audit_Evidence.md using Xvfb, Tcl/Tk 9.0.4 and the recorded dependencies.
expected: The manager settles within the bounded drain at all tested scalings, without geometry feedback starving useful UI work.
actual: Assertion 20000 not less than 20000 at scaling 1.25; 1 failed in 3.06s. Fontconfig cache warning also present. No Windows/customer-EXE reproduction was performed.
v69: Related geometry-loop exposure existed in v0.9.69; this new test is absent there. Do not call the exact failure a proven new v0.9.70 regression.
regression: Repeat on packaged Windows/Tk and Linux at 100–200% scaling, with actual event/geometry traces; verify Finish commits before refresh and remains responsive.
fix: Investigate the remaining geometry feedback under the recorded environment; fix only after tracing it. Keep bounded tests; do not infer a persistence fix from UI responsiveness alone.
recovery: A UI stall after Finish can occur after commit. Inspect preserved copies for the polygon record before assuming loss or re-digitizing; force-killing can discard other pending memory edits.
